description: NaLi₃GeO₄ is Aluminum carbonitride-derived structured and crystallizes in the tetragonal I4₁/a space group. Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.46-2.83 Å. There are three inequivalent Li sites. In the first Li site, Li is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted LiO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent LiO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four equivalent LiO₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Li-O bond distances ranging from 1.88-2.20 Å. In the second Li site, Li is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted LiO₄ trigonal pyramids that share corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with six LiO₄ tetrahedra,  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one GeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Li-O bond distances ranging from 1.93-2.19 Å. In the third Li site, Li is bonded to four O atoms to form LiO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent LiO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent LiO₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are three shorter (1.98 Å) and one longer (2.05 Å) Li-O bond length. Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with six LiO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent LiO₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one LiO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are three shorter (1.78 Å) and one longer (1.79 Å) Ge-O bond length. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to one Na, three Li, and one Ge atom to form distorted corner-sharing ONaLi₃Ge trigonal bipyramids. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, three Li, and one Ge atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to one Na, three Li, and one Ge atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, three Li, and one Ge atom.
